project-card.summary: The project card: the only per-project input error-sweep takes. Required fields, where the card lives, why it stays out of a public repo, and the rule for where a learned gotcha goes (adapter vs card vs shared skill). Drifts whenever the pipeline or an adapter changes what it reads off the card.

docs-sweep-card.summary: The roster card: the only input docs-sweep takes. One card for the whole fleet, its fields (repos root, worktrees root, excludes, extra repos, PR cap, branch prefix, per-repo overrides), where it lives, why it stays out of a public repo, and the rule for where a learned gotcha goes (card vs pipeline). Drifts whenever the pipeline changes what it reads off the card.

coderabbit-sweep-card.summary: The fleet card: the only input coderabbit-sweep takes. One card per account rather than per repo (the review allowance is per developer), its fields (owner, excluded repos and PRs, drafts, trigger phrase, cooldown, ledger, report), and the rule for where a learned gotcha goes (card vs pipeline). Drifts whenever the pipeline changes what it reads off the card.

ga-traffic-report-card.summary: The report card: the only input ga-traffic-report takes. Its fields (data folder, artifact, time zone, parked sites, plain and full audit cadence, max audits per run, credit floor), where it lives and why it stays out of a public repo. Drifts whenever the pipeline changes what it reads off the card.

index-sweep-card.summary: The fleet card: the only input index-sweep takes. One card for every site, in priority order, with its fields (per-site cap, drip days, minimum gap, resend limit, cool-off, campaign name, low-credit floor, run log, and per-site sitemap, OpenSEO project ID and skip patterns), why it stays out of a public repo, and the rule for where a learned gotcha goes. Drifts whenever the pipeline changes what it reads off the card.

sync-docs.summary: The doc-key mechanism and the shared sync-docs skill: what a doc key is, how to tag a source, how to register a page, what config.json and rules.md hold, what each check reports, how a repo adopts the skill, and how to run it in audit vs fix scope.
